MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  LA VERNE HELD IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  OF THE LA VERNE CITY HALL
  Monday, April 1, 2019

1  A regular meeting of the La Verne City Council was called to order by Mayor Kendrick at 6: 30 p. m.

2  Council Members present:  Mayor Don Kendrick
  Mayor Pro Tern Charlie Rosales
  Council Member Robin Carder
  Council Member Tim Hepburn
  Council Member Muir Davis

  Absent:  None.

  Advisory personnel present:  City Manager Robert Russi
  City Attorney Robert L. Kress
  Assistant City Manager/ Public Works Director Dan Keesey
  Assistant City Clerk Lupe Gaeta Estrella
  Community Development Director Eric Scherer
  Community Services Director Bill Aguirre
  Police Chief Nick Paz
  Police Lieutenant Sam Gonzalez
  Personnel Officer JR Ranells
  Assistant Planner Maia McCurley

3.  Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Kendrick.

4..  Presentation  of  Proclamation  Mayor Kendrick, on behalf of the City Council, presented a Proclamation
  Declaring  the  Month  of April,  declaring the Month of April, 2019, DMV/ Donate Life California Month to
  2019,  DMV/ Donate  Life  Donate Life Ambassador Brenda Yunt.
  California Month

  Donate Life Ambassador Brenda Yunt thanked the City Council and spoke
  about the Donate Life California organization and the importance of being a
  donor.

  Presentation on the 2020  Michael Khouri, a Partnership Specialist from the Los Angeles Regional Census
  Census  Center gave an update on current efforts related to the 2020 Census, along with
  a slide presentation. He also provided information on ways the members of the
  La Verne community can get involved and assist in the Census efforts. In
  addition, he reported that the County of Los Angeles has created a Complete
  Count Committee.

5.  Consent Calendar  It was moved by Carder, seconded by Rosales, and unanimously carried to
  accept, approve, or act on the Consent Calendar items, except for the
  following items were pulled for further discussion.

  City Council Minutes of March 4, 2019
  Register of Audited Demands
 City Council Minutes, Monday, April 1, 2019, Page 2

Pulled from Consent Calendar  Pam Berry and Richard Bowen, La Verne residents requested the Minutes of
for Discussion/ City Council  March 4, 2019, be pulled for discussion.
Minutes
  Pam Berry, La Verne resident read La Verne' s Press Release regarding the
  tentative settlement reached with the La Verne Firefighters' Lawsuit. She
  stated that in the Mayor' s statement, he did not state a certain section of the
  press release as noted in the minutes of March 4, 2019. She stated that the
  minutes are incorrect.

  Richard Bowen, La Verne resident agreed that the March 4, 2019, City Council
  minutes were incorrect and that the Mayor never said the second paragraph of
  the Press Release as noted in the minutes. He stated it never happened. He
  asked what are the purpose of minutes and how are they processed . He stated
  that the minutes should be amended.

  City Manager Russi agreed that the Mayor did not state the second paragraph
  of the Press Release at the March 4, 2019, Council meeting and that the
  minutes will be amended.

  It was moved Carder and seconded by Hepburn to amend the City Council
  Minutes of March 4, 2019, by deleting the statement of the second paragraph
  of the Press Release not stated by the Mayor regarding the tentative
  settlement reached with the La Verne Firefighters' Lawsuit .

Pulled from the Consent  Register of Audited Demands was pulled by La Verne resident Fred Faught for
Calendar for  discussion and information.
discussion/ Registers of Audited
Demands  Fred Faught, La Verne resident, questioned the payment to Wallin, Kress,
  Reisman and Kranitz in the amount of$ 17, 188. 09 and asked if there was an
  itemized list of services rendered by the firm. In addition he questioned
  payment to the Superior Courts of California, Los Angeles in the amount of
  5, 606. 00.

  City Manager Russi and Finance Manager Statham replied that the payment to
  Superior Court was for the Court' s portion of the parking citations fees and he
  was told to contact the Finance Department in regards to the Wallin, Kress,
  Reisman, and Reisman invoice.

  It was moved by Carder, seconded by Hepburn, and unanimously carried to
  approve the Register of Audited Demands, as follows:

  In the amount of$ 897, 654. 24, dated March 13, 2019, and
  In the amount of$ 761, 170. 14, dated March 20, 2019.

Street Closure for the Cool  Street Closure for the Cool Cruise Car Show. Case No. 22- 19SEP - The
Cruise Car Show, Case No.  City Council was requested to consider a street closure for the Cool Cruise
22- 19SEP  Car Show on April 20, 2019. Flying Deuces submitted a request to close
  Third Street from B to E Streets and D Street from Second Street to
  Bonita Avenue.  The street closure will be between the hours of 5: 00 a. m.
  and  5: 00 p. m. the day  of  the  event.  There are expected to be over 500
  cars parked on the closed sections of the street, as well as various University
  of La Verne  parking lots.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, April 1, 2019, Page 3

  Staff recommended that the City Council approve a minute motion directing
  the Public Works Director to take the necessary steps to permit the
  temporary street closure for portions of D and Third Streets in Old Town
  La Verne; and approve to waive administrative review fees necessary for the
  processing, permitting, management, promotion, and operations of the Cool
  Cruise Car Show; with exception to the payment to the La Verne Police
  Department Reserves. Approved as recommended.

  Resolution ( s)  passed &  adopted, as recommended, as follows:

  Resolution  No. 19- 14,  Resolution  No. 19- 14 -  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  Authorizing  Execution of an  THE CITY OF LA VERNE, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF
  Agreement with Athens  CALIFORNIA, AUTHORIZING EXECUTION OF AN AGREEMENT
  Services for Street Sweeping  BETWEEN THE CITY OF LA VERNE AND ATHENS SERVICES FOR
  Services in the City of  STREET SWEEPING SERVICES - The Public Works Department solicited
  La Verne  a Request for Proposals ( RFP) for Street Sweeping Services in 2018 in
  accordance with the City Council approved Fiscal Sustainability program. This
  service is intended to replace the current in- house street sweeping program
  and expected to save the City about$ 125, 000 annually. Award of a contract
  was anticipated in October, of 2018, but delayed to allow staff to evaluate a
  proposal from Waste Management to include such services within their
  existing refuse contract. Staff negotiated a monthly payment from Waste
  Management to compensate the City for costs incurred in delaying the
  contract award. Waste Management eventually concluded that incorporation
  of sweeping services into their existing contract would not be practical. As
  such, staff forwarded a recommendation for the award of a contract for street
  sweeping services in the City of La Verne per the June 2018 RFP. This project
  is categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act.

  Staff recommended that the City Council approve Resolution No. 19- 14, which
  awards a  public services contract to Athens Services in the initial amount
  of$ 102, 061. 80 for street sweeping services in the City of La Verne. Approved
  as recommended by staff.

6.  Public Comment  This was the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the City Council on
  items not listed in any other place on the agenda. Mayor Kendrick called for
  public comment.

  Virgie Beltran, La Verne resident, stated that her family was being targeted by
  law enforcement and that it was not right. She stated that rookie police officers
  are targeting her family and questioned if they were trained to work with the
  mentally ill. She stated she would not stand for this to happen in her City
  where she was born and raised.

  Joyce Kelly, La Verne resident asked what the status of videotaping of Council
  meetings was.

  City Attorney Kress stated the contract is being reviewed and installation of
  equipment should by the next fiscal year and videotaping by August or
  September, of 2019.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, April 1, 2019, Page 4

  Richard Bowen, La Verne resident, thanked Police Chief Paz for attending the
  La Verne Coalition of Concerned Citizens ( LV3C) meeting. He thanked
  Finance Manger Statham and Public Works Director Keesey for meeting with
  him regarding the mid- year reports. He stated he read Council Member
  Carder' s statement in the minutes regarding the Council medical coverage and
  why it was extended. He stated that it still did not answer his question on why
  the vote was overridden and who are" they", as referred in Council Member'
  Carder' s statement. He asked where the documentation is ( which he has
  asked for months) that authorized the change on this matter. He stated he
  received the City Manager' s Briefing where it made reference to the change,
  but it did not recommend or approve the change.

  Barbara, League of Women Voters, thanked the City Council for the census
  count presentation. She spoke about the importance of Census count and that
  everyone should be counted. She stated she was pleased that Los Angeles
  County has created a Complete Count Committee and she would be happy to
  work with them.

7.  Council Comments and  Council Member Hepburn congratulated Sabina Sullivan for being named
  Meeting/ Conference Reports  La Verne' s 2019 Woman of Distinction by Assembly Member Holden. He
  thanked Police Chief Paz, Captain Flores, Police Sargent Leeper and
  Community Services Officer Savage for attending the La Verne Coalition of
  Concerned Citizens ( LV3C) meeting. He stated they were very informative
  especially on the issue of Homelessness and how La Verne is dealing with it.
  He stated that Tri- City Mental Health Agency offers a lot of services for the
  homeless and works closely with the La Verne Police Department. He stated
  they do an amazing job working together. He reported on the University of
  La Verne 2019 Scholarship Gala and that it was a nice event. He spoke about
  the La Verne Historical Society and the work they do. He stated that he left
  flyers for membership to the La Verne Historical Society and encouraged
  people to join. He stated the La Verne Historical Society does a wonderful job
  and sponsors many functions and that preserving the history of La Verne is
  important. He also reported on the Gold Line meeting which will be held on
  Tuesday, April 16, 2019, at the La Verne Community Center and encouraged
  people to attend.

  Council Member Davis also thanked the La Verne Police Department for
  attending the La Verne Coalition of Concerned Citizens ( LV3C) meeting and
  for the very informative presentation. He reported on the Tax Measure
  meeting and there was a lot of good discussion at the meeting. He thanked
  those individuals who attended the meeting. He also reported on the La Verne
  San Dimas Educational Golf Tournament to be held on April 26, 2019 and
  invited the public to sign up and support our schools. He also stated that the
  Census Count is important and it would be awesome that La Verne count is
  close to 100 percent.

  Council Member Carder reported on the La Verne Police Officers' Association
  Golf Tournament on May 20, 2019 and that the proceeds from the event will go
  to the Youth and Family Action Committee. She stated she sits on the Tri- City
  Mental Health Board and knows that the La Verne Police Officers are trained
  to deal with the homeless.  She stated that La Verne Sargent Leeper works
  closely with Tri- City Mental Health. She said that public safety is the number
  one concern. In addition, she reported on the La Verne/ San Dimas Home
  Town Heroes event honoring first responders in the community on
  Wednesday, May 8, 2019, and invited people to attend to thank and honor
  La Verne' s own.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, April 1, 2019, Page 5

  Mayor Kendrick reported on the City' s State of the City Address which was
  held on March 21, 2019 and sponsored by La Verne Rotary Club and the
  La Verne Chamber of Commerce. He also reported on Grace Miller
  Elementary students who toured City Hall and staged mock council meetings
  and on the University of La Verne 2019 Scholarship Gala. He stated that half
  of the students are the first in their families to go to College and praised the
  scholarship program which helps these students get an education without
  going into debt.

8  Adjournment at 7: 31 pm.

  Respectfully submitted,
